content.text:
Confirmed: [Discussion #13184](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13184) reports a real regression introduced by [PR #13131](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13131) in v2026.9.7. There are currently no replies.

I reproduced it on current `main` with an isolated environment and `npm:cowsay@1.6.0`:

```text
mise ⇢ npm:cowsay@1.6.0 · already installed
mise WARN  missing: npm:cowsay@1.6.0
1.6.0
```

Every subsequent `mise exec` repeats the install check and warning, while `mise ls` reports `installed: true, active: true` and `mise which` resolves the executable correctly.

The root cause is [src/backend/npm.rs:501](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/98cf/mise/src/backend/npm.rs:501). An npm request without an attached aube graph is declared unsatisfied whenever the merged `Settings` says lockfile creation is enabled:

```rust
!tv.resolved_from_lockfile() && Settings::get().lockfile_creation_enabled()
```

A project’s `lockfile = true` enters that merged setting, even when the npm request belongs to the global config. This contradicts the lockfile ownership rules in [src/lockfile.rs:2508](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/98cf/mise/src/lockfile.rs:2508), which explicitly avoid automatically creating global lockfiles.

Running `mise lock --global` made the reproduction immediately silent, confirming that the missing owner-specific graph is the distinction—not the physical installation.

The fix should make the “graph required” decision relative to the request’s owning lockfile rather than the merged project setting. Care is needed to preserve:

- Existing revision-2 lockfiles that need graphs.
- Project configs explicitly opting into automatic lockfile creation.
- The legacy `MISE_LOCKFILE=1` behavior.
- Global lockfiles remaining opt-in through `mise lock --global`.

An e2e regression test should install a global-only npm tool, enable lockfiles in a separate project, and assert repeated `mise exec` and `mise install --dry-run` remain satisfied. The existing npm graph tests cover project tools but not this global/project ownership boundary.

No repository changes or GitHub replies were made.
make a pr, post a reply
I’ll turn the confirmed ownership bug into a focused regression fix, run the npm/lockfile checks, open a review-ready PR, then re-read the discussion immediately before posting the public reply.

Projects with `lockfile = true` currently make npm tools declared only in the global config appear missing because the project lockfile setting incorrectly requires those global requests to carry an embedded-aube dependency graph. Every `mise exec` consequently performs an install pass, reports the physically present tool as already installed, and then warns that the same tool is missing.

This keeps automatic graph creation scoped to non-global requests. A project lockfile no longer changes the installation state of an npm tool owned by the global config, while npm entries actually resolved from revision 2 lockfiles continue to require and replay their stored graphs.

For example, with a global pin:

```toml
[tools]
"npm:xcodebuildmcp" = "2.7.0"
```

and a project setting:

```toml
[settings]
lockfile = true
```

`mise exec` now reuses the installed global tool without a redundant install pass or `missing` warning. Users who want the global tool graph-locked can still opt in explicitly with `mise lock --global`.

The regression test covers both `mise install --dry-run` and `mise exec` across this global/project ownership boundary. This also includes the rustls 0.23.45 lockfile update from 9fe9c9c998919597093669f05c4853a58fe8c127 so CI does not fail on RUSTSEC-2026-0285.

Conclusion: the implementation is still the right boundary, but my explanation was wrong.

`lockfile = true` is a global merged setting. The fix is justified because automatic lock maintenance has separately excluded global tool sources since #8707, and #11746 preserved that rule when it added automatic project-lockfile creation. The new npm graph code accidentally created a graph-specific install for a global request even though no automatic path could ever write that graph to the global lockfile.

I’m correcting the PR/discussion language to say “automatic lockfile target policy,” and I’ll add a short code comment so this does not look like invented project-local setting semantics.

const r = await tools.write_stdin({
  session_id: 94515,
  chars: `\`lockfile = true\` is an invocation-wide setting, but automatic lockfile maintenance deliberately excludes tools owned by global configs. Global lockfiles and their dependency data are only created explicitly with \`mise lock --global\`.

The new embedded-aube graph path did not preserve that distinction. When lockfiles were enabled, it generated a graph-specific installation identity for an unlocked npm request from the global config. No automatic flow could persist that graph to the owning global lockfile, so the next \`mise exec\` resolved the same request without a graph, treated the physically present tool as unsatisfied, performed a redundant install pass, and warned that it was missing.

Automatic graph creation now follows the existing lockfile-target policy: unlocked non-global requests can receive graphs for automatic project-lockfile maintenance, while global requests remain version-only unless they are actually resolved from an explicitly generated revision 2 global lockfile. This does not introduce project-local semantics for \`[settings]\`.

For example, with a global pin:

\`\`\`toml
[tools]
"npm:xcodebuildmcp" = "2.7.0"
\`\`\`

and \`lockfile = true\` enabled anywhere in the merged settings, \`mise exec\` now reuses the installed global tool without a redundant install pass or \`missing\` warning. Users who want that global tool graph-locked can opt in with \`mise lock --global\`.

The regression test covers both \`mise install --dry-run\` and \`mise exec\` across the global-source/automatic-lockfile boundary. This also includes the rustls 0.23.45 lockfile update from 9fe9c9c998919597093669f05c4853a58fe8c127 so CI does not fail on RUSTSEC-2026-0285.

You were right: there is no separately scoped “project `lockfile = true`” setting.

A project `mise.toml` can contain `[settings] lockfile = true`, which enables automatic project-lockfile creation, but settings are merged invocation-wide. The separate policy is:

- Automatic maintenance targets project lockfiles.
- Global lockfiles require `mise lock --global`.
- `[tool_config] locked = true` is the config-root-scoped strict-locking mechanism.

That matches [Discussion #8663](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/8663), [PR #8707](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/8707), [Discussion #11739](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/11739), [PR #11746](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/11746), [PR #11940](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/11940), and the current [lockfile documentation](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/mise-lock.html).
